what_its_for: Rivaroxaban is a blood thinner (anticoagulant) used to prevent or treat blood clots. Your doctor may have prescribed it to reduce your risk of stroke if you have an irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation), to treat or prevent a blood clot in your leg (deep vein thrombosis or DVT) or lungs (pulmonary embolism), or to lower your risk of serious heart problems if you have coronary or peripheral artery disease.
how_to_take: Take rivaroxaban exactly as your doctor tells you. If you are taking the 15 mg or 20 mg dose, always take it WITH your evening meal — food helps your body absorb the medicine properly. The 2.5 mg and 10 mg doses can be taken with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. If you have trouble swallowing, you may crush the tablet and mix it with a small amount of applesauce, then take it right away followed by food. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can raise your risk of a blood clot or stroke.
dosing: Your dose depends on the reason you are taking it and your kidney function. Common doses are: 20 mg once daily with the evening meal for atrial fibrillation; 15 mg twice daily with meals for the first 3 weeks of DVT/PE treatment, then 20 mg once daily with the evening meal; 10 mg once daily for DVT prevention after hip or knee surgery; 2.5 mg twice daily (with or without food) when combined with aspirin for heart or artery disease. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the SAME DAY. If you are on the twice-daily dose (15 mg twice daily), you may take two tablets at once to make up for the missed dose. If you are on a once-daily dose and you don't remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose. Never take a double dose to make up for a missed one unless your doctor tells you otherwise. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store rivaroxaban at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Store it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or other NSAIDs (anti-inflammatory pain relievers) unless your doctor specifically told you to, as these increase your risk of serious bleeding. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol (limit yourself to 1–2 drinks per day at most), as it raises your bleeding risk. Tell your doctor or dentist that you take a blood thinner before any surgery, dental procedure, or medical test. Be extra careful to avoid cuts and injuries. Use a soft toothbrush and an electric razor to reduce bleeding risk. Avoid herbal supplements like St. John's Wort, ginkgo biloba, and garlic supplements, as they can interact with this medication.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you notice: unusual bruising or bleeding that won't stop; pink, red, or dark brown urine; red or black tarry stools; coughing or vomiting up blood; severe headache, dizziness, or weakness; pain or swelling in a joint; cuts that won't stop bleeding; or heavy or unexpected menstrual bleeding. Also tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, or if you need any surgery or procedure. Call your doctor before starting any new prescription medicine, over-the-counter medication, vitamin, or herbal supplement.
when_it_works: Rivaroxaban starts working within 2 to 4 hours after you take your first dose. It is important to take it every day as prescribed to keep it working properly. You may not feel any different while taking it — that is normal. The medicine is working in the background to prevent dangerous blood clots, so do not stop taking it just because you feel fine.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if your kidneys are not working well, since rivaroxaban is partly removed from the body through the kidneys. Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease. Liver problems: Rivaroxaban is NOT recommended if you have significant liver disease. Tell your doctor about any liver problems. Older adults: Older patients may have a higher risk of bleeding and should be monitored closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Rivaroxaban is NOT safe to use during pregnancy as it can harm the baby, and it should not be used while breastfeeding. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, may become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children for most conditions — check with your doctor.
